mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS suggests growing labor market strength, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payrolls momentum is not statistically predictive of SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.01, p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening supply-side demand, which raises the cost of capital and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% from the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the mean when INDPRO is contracting (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal persistent demand pressures that prompt preemptive equity reallocation away from growth sectors, yielding negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positively correlated with CPIAUCSL change (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5%, it triggers a shift in risk-free rates that elevates the discount rate for equities, producing a negative 60-day forward return for the S&P 500.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between FEDFUNDS crossing and SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) followed by a decline suggests a cooling labor market, lowering investor sentiment and pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases then decreases in the same month
failure_condition: PAYEMS volatility is not predictive of SPX returns (interaction p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence, so this sketch is invalid - must be discarded) - wait, can't use unavailable proxies. Alternative: Concurrent declines in supply indicators (INDPRO and RSAFS) indicate oversupply conditions that suppress equity valuations, producing negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negatively correlated with the combined INDPRO-RSAFS signal (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation expectations (implied by CPIAUCSL trajectory), a persistent rise in FEDFUNDS above 5% produces a term premium effect that compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are in the specified regime (p > 0.05).
